A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ASTRA with the same authors and core framework. All 19 pages of each version, including appendix equations, tables, plots and qualitative examples, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original defense, utility, transferability and ablation experiments on MiniGPT-4, Qwen2-VL and LLaVA-v1.5, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds attack-transfer and harmless-prompt compliance results in Tables 5 and 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects its stated surrogate-target computation from probability to log probability, matching the definition already present in Section 3.1. The attribution, vector construction, calibration and adaptive-steering procedures otherwise remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v3 adds XSTest evaluation of excessive refusal on harmless prompts and JailbreakBench-based OOD evaluation, including text-only GCG attacks. This substantially extends coverage beyond the earlier visual-attack transfer tests and general vision-language utility benchmarks.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 8 retain Self-reminder, JailGuard, ECSO, Refusal Pairs and Jailbreak Templates. Transferability and utility comparisons still compare ASTRA with undefended models. The added attack algorithms extend testing conditions without changing defense-comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported attribution instruction pool changes from 831 AdvBench/Anthropic-HHH instructions to 416 AdvBench instructions, and ID construction/test images change from distinct to the same ImageNet classes. OOD testing now uses 55 JailbreakBench prompts and two perturbation budgets per visual attack. XSTest introduces 250 safe prompts scored through string-matched compliance. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 5 expands robustness testing to Auto-PGD, MI-FGSM and text-only GCG, while XSTest directly probes excessive refusal. Existing adaptive-attack tests, component ablations, coefficient/image-count/layer analyses and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without evaluation confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-based uncertainty reporting. The three image-attribution passes per image are unchanged construction details, not newly reported repeated evaluations.

E6.justification: Table 5 replaces the earlier four-budget OOD PGD block with revised PGD and additional attack results. Newly reported MiniGPT-4 GCG ASR is 58.18% without defense versus 9.09% with ASTRA. Table 6 adds XSTest scores. These are new or replaced results under revised conditions; Tables 1–4 and 7–9, retained utility scores and existing ablation plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 repairs the probability versus log-probability inconsistency with Section 3.1's existing definition of f(g). This is a limited formal correction; the steering-vector and calibrated-projection equations are otherwise equivalent, with no added assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and third contribution explicitly extend the transferability claim to PGD variants and text-only attacks. The central claims about ASTRA's defense effectiveness, utility preservation and efficiency remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The shared harmful-direction interpretation, visual-versus-textual mechanism discussion and explanation of utility preservation are retained. Both versions acknowledge weaker transfer from unconstrained-image steering vectors to constrained attacks; no substantive new limitations are introduced.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link, specifies the 416/415 dataset breakdown of the 831 PGD optimization pairs, and adds a data-flow diagram. Hardware, software and steering hyperparameters remain unchanged. The new Figure 4 introduces an inconsistency by showing 17 construction images while Sections 4.1 and 4.4 state 16.

R1.justification: Six references are added, covering JailbreakBench, XSTest, Auto-PGD, momentum attacks, a trustworthiness survey and ALI-Agent. The related-work narrative and positioning relative to VLM defenses and textual activation steering remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental setup and transferability passages receive localized rewrites, and appendix terminology clarifies that training-set size means images used for steering-vector construction. An acknowledgment section is added, while the main narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the data-flow Figure 4, expands Tables 5 and 6, moves table captions above tables and relocates retained appendix figures. It also wraps the mean-difference equation that overflowed into the adjacent column in v1. Existing method diagrams, plots and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded attack tests and direct XSTest assessment provide better evidence for transferability and utility preservation. The code link, pseudocode correction and repaired equation layout also improve usability. These gains are limited by unexplained revisions to attribution and ID settings and the new 17-versus-16 image-count inconsistency. Overall, v3 provides a useful incremental improvement to an otherwise largely retained paper.
